deals.retailCotenants: Grocery Outlet is one of only two grocers serving the New Cumberland trade area. Competing retail concentrations within 5 miles include Capital City Mall, Camp Hill Shopping Center and High Point Commons. Capital City Airport is adjacent.

tenants.name: Grocery Outlet
tenants.rentSchedule: Flat $14.13/SF ($235,265) in CY2027 through the October 2030 expiry. The OM does not print the step schedule or the option structure.
tenants.renewalOptions: Not disclosed in the OM — pull the lease. A grocery lease signed in November 2025 would normally carry several five-year options.
tenants.parentCompany: Grocery Outlet Holding Corp. (store operated by an independent local owner-operator — confirm the contracting entity)
tenants.assumptionNote: THE ANCHOR AND THE REASON TO LOOK. 33% of GLA, 45% of base rent, 44% of total tenant revenue, with $14.2 million of sales ($853 PSF) at a computed 2.16% occupancy cost (base $235,265 + recoveries $71,396 / $14.2M) — outstanding productivity, and one of only two grocers serving the New Cumberland trade area. Unlike the other grocers in this portfolio, the rent is NOT below market: $14.13/SF against CBRE's own $15.00/SF assumption for this suite, so this is fairly-priced income rather than mark-to-market depth. TWO THINGS TO VERIFY. First, the lease commenced 1 NOVEMBER 2025 and runs only to October 2030 — a five-year primary term on a brand-new grocery lease is unusually short, so the option structure (not disclosed here) is what actually determines the hold-period income; get it. Second, Grocery Outlet's model is INDEPENDENT LOCAL OWNER-OPERATORS who control inventory, hiring and marketing — confirm whether the lease is with Grocery Outlet Holding Corp. or with the operator entity, and whether any corporate guaranty exists. CBRE excludes the grocer from the general vacancy-loss factor.

otherIncome.note: Flat $8,400/year, modeled with NO growth across the entire 11-year projection — a licence fee, not contractual rent. It is 1.7% of NOI. Confirm the agreement's term and cancellability; a month-to-month donation-bin licence should not be capitalized at the same rate as rent.

keyAssumptions: ROSTER BASIS: CBRE's IN-PLACE PRO-FORMA for calendar year 2027 (page 9), which is what the $492,981 in-place NOI, the $174,188 recovery line and the $702,350 effective gross revenue tie to. This OM prints FULL lease dates (MM/DD/YY), so no date convention was needed. Where the page-4 site plan shows a lower CURRENT rate, that rate is recorded in each tenant's rentSchedule.

Four-way tie-out against the OM's printed totals: (a) 40,515 SF occupied + 9,970 SF vacant = 50,485 SF GLA; (b) 40,515 / 50,485 = 80.3% occupancy; (c) base rents sum to $519,762 = the printed Total Tenant Revenue Occupied; (d) $702,350 EGR - $209,369 OpEx = $492,981 NOI. Tenant recoveries sum to $174,187 vs the $174,188 printed (rounding).
WALT computes to 4.46 years from the roster's expiries SF-weighted as of 01/01/2027, reproducing the OM's stated +/-4.5 years — an independent confirmation the roster is complete.

THE $8,400 PLANET AID PARKING LICENCE is real income but is NOT rent: it is a donation-bin licence, modeled flat with zero growth across all eleven projection years. It is inside the $702,350 EGR and therefore inside the $492,981 NOI. At 1.7% of NOI it is not material to value, but confirm its term and cancellability rather than capitalizing it like a lease.

GROCERY OUTLET'S LEASE IS BRAND NEW AND SHORT: commenced 1 November 2025, primary term to 31 October 2030 — five years on a grocery anchor that is 45% of base rent. The OM does not disclose the option structure, which is what actually governs income beyond 2030. This is the single most important missing document in the deal.

GROCERY OUTLET OPERATES THROUGH INDEPENDENT LOCAL OWNER-OPERATORS who control each store's inventory, hiring and marketing (the OM says so on page 2). Confirm whether the lease is with Grocery Outlet Holding Corp. or with the local operator entity, and whether a corporate guaranty exists — the credit answer differs enormously between the two.
NO PRICE AND NO CAP RATE are quoted — unpriced marketing package. Value must be underwritten off the $492,981 in-place NOI.

TAXES ARE NOT REASSESSED, AND THIS IS PENNSYLVANIA — the state where our tax-reassessment work has found the most value and the most risk. The $61,006 CY2027 tax line is the 2026 budget grown 3% annually; the OM states expressly that reassessment is the investor's responsibility. Cumberland County uses a stale base-year assessment adjusted by an annually-republished Common Level Ratio, so the exposure here is NOT an automatic sale-price reset but an assessment appeal or CLR movement. Verify the current-year Cumberland County CLR (republished each July) and the property's base-year assessment before bidding. At $1.21/SF the modeled tax line is low for a Pennsylvania retail center and is 12% of NOI.

CBRE MODELS A 16-MONTH ABSORPTION WINDOW for the 9,970 SF of vacancy (1/1/2027 to 5/1/2028) — longer than the 12 months used elsewhere in this portfolio, which is an honest acknowledgment that 8,780 SF of it is junior-box rather than small-shop space.

TWO 2026 LEASES AND A 2024 LEASE UNDERCUT CBRE'S SMALL-SHOP MARKET RENT. Ella Rose Massage signed in April 2026 at $17.50/SF and Divine Thread signed in April 2024 at $16.00/SF, both below the $20.00/SF CBRE assumes for sub-2,000 SF space; Sophia's Pizzeria signed in November 2024 at $16.36/SF against a $16.50/SF assumption for 2,000-5,000 SF space, which does validate the mid-size assumption. Weigh the actual signings, not just the assumption sheet, when underwriting the lease-up.

The OM does not print a year built, a renovation year, individual rent steps, renewal-option terms, or any co-tenancy, exclusive or kickout clause. All left null rather than estimated. No footer date stamp appears on the Fairview pro-forma pages, so omDate is left null (the sister Project Evergreen books are stamped July-August 2026).

redFlags.description: THE ANCHOR'S PRIMARY TERM RUNS OUT IN OCTOBER 2030 AND THE OPTIONS ARE UNDISCLOSED. Grocery Outlet signed on 1 November 2025 for only five years and is 33% of GLA, 45% of base rent and 44% of tenant revenue. A five-year primary term on a new grocery lease is short, and everything about the hold-period income beyond 2030 depends on an option structure the OM never prints. Get the lease before anything else.

19.7% VACANT, AND 8,780 SF OF IT IS JUNIOR-BOX SPACE (suites 011 and 012), not small-shop fill. CBRE itself models a 16-month absorption window rather than the 12 months used elsewhere in this portfolio. The entire value-add case — NOI growing 85.5% over ten years, from $488,776 in CY2027 to $906,594 by CY2036 — rests on leasing that space, and the CY2028 capital line carries $359,419 of TI plus $55,341 of commissions to do it.

GROCERY OUTLET'S CREDIT MAY NOT BE GROCERY OUTLET. The chain operates through independent local owner-operators who control inventory, hiring and marketing. Unless the lease is signed by Grocery Outlet Holding Corp. or corporately guaranteed, the covenant behind 45% of the base rent is a single local operator, not a 550-store public company. The OM does not say which.

TWO OF THE THREE HIGHEST RENTS AT THE CENTER LOOK ABOVE MARKET AND HAVE NO SALES TO SUPPORT THEM. Smoker's Express pays $26.18/SF against CBRE's own $20.00/SF market rent for space that size — 31% above — on a tobacco use, and Fashion Nails pays $20.56/SF. Meanwhile three leases actually signed in 2024-2026 came in at $16.00-$17.50/SF. Above-market rent inflates the NOI a buyer capitalizes and can reset DOWN at renewal; Smoker's Express reaches its expiry in October 2029, inside the hold.

PENNSYLVANIA PROPERTY-TAX EXPOSURE IS UNMODELED. The $61,006 tax line is $1.21/SF — low for a PA retail center — and is expressly not reassessed. Cumberland County runs a stale base-year assessment adjusted by an annually-republished Common Level Ratio, so the risk is an appeal or CLR movement rather than an automatic sale reset. Verify the current CLR and base-year assessment; this is the state where that work matters most.

NO SALES ARE DISCLOSED FOR ANY TENANT EXCEPT GROCERY OUTLET. Ten of eleven occupied suites have no productivity data, including Smoker's Express and Fashion Nails, the two rows whose rents look most stretched.

Dollar Tree recovers only $3.54/SF against the center's $4.84-$5.02/SF shop rate on 21.4% of the GLA — a capped structure that leaves ownership carrying part of the expense growth, PA taxes included, on the second-largest suite.

The tenant roster outside Grocery Outlet and Dollar Tree is entirely local operators and franchisees — no investment-grade tenancy, no disclosed guaranties, and two seasonal or regulatory-sensitive uses (Jackson Hewitt, Smoker's Express).

upsideItems.detail: Lease up 9,970 SF across three suites (19.7% of GLA) — the dominant driver of CBRE's 85.5% ten-year NOI growth and 6.53% CAGR. NOI is modeled to jump from $488,776 in CY2027 to $680,675 in CY2028 on that absorption alone. Budget the $359,419 of CY2028 TI and $55,341 of commissions against it, and note CBRE allowed 16 months rather than 12 because 8,780 SF of it is junior-box space.

upsideItems.item: Grocery Outlet does $853 PSF at a 2.16% occupancy cost
upsideItems.detail: Grocery Outlet is an outstanding store: $14.2 million of sales, $853 PSF, at a computed 2.16% occupancy cost — among the strongest grocery productivity in this entire portfolio group — in a trade area served by only two grocers. That performance is what makes the 2030 option decision very likely to go the landlord's way, once the option terms are known.

upsideItems.item: Jackson Hewitt is 50% below market and rolls in 2030
upsideItems.detail: Jackson Hewitt at $10.48/SF against a $20.00/SF market rent for space that size is the deepest single shop mark-to-market in the deal, and it expires May 2030 — inside a normal hold. LHM Physical Therapy at $15.12/SF against $16.50/SF adds a smaller increment in June 2029.

upsideItems.item: Dollar Tree is deeply below market but locked to 2033
upsideItems.detail: Dollar Tree at $6.00/SF against CBRE's $9.00/SF assumption for that suite is 50% below market on 21.4% of the GLA. It is secure, very sticky income from an investment-grade credit in place 25 years — but the December 2033 expiry sits beyond a normal 5-7 year hold, so treat it as durability rather than capturable upside.

A genuinely strong and high-barrier trade area for a center this size: 63,350 people within three miles at a $91,662 average household income, and a true trade area of 44,800 people at $117,595 average income and $98,189 median. New Cumberland is a dense, historic, built-out suburb directly across the Susquehanna from the state capital — supply is constrained, which supports both rents and a tighter going-in cap than the headline NOI alone suggests.

upsideItems.item: Between I-83 and the PA Turnpike
upsideItems.detail: Superior commuter and logistics positioning between I-83 (36,700 AADT) and the Pennsylvania Turnpike (42,500 AADT), across the river from Harrisburg and within reach of York, Carlisle, Mechanicsburg and Hershey — a daytime population of 81,457 within three miles against a resident population of 63,350.

upsideItems.item: Dairy Queen holds a drive-thru through 2032
upsideItems.detail: Dairy Queen holds a drive-thru position through August 2032 — the most valuable and least replaceable small-shop configuration at the center.

deals.notes: Fairview Commons is a 50,485 SF Grocery Outlet-anchored neighborhood center on Old York Road in New Cumberland, Pennsylvania — a dense, built-out, high-barrier suburb directly across the Susquehanna River from Harrisburg — offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. It is 80.3% leased and produces $492,981 of CY2027 in-place NOI on $702,350 of effective gross revenue against $209,369 of operating expenses, at a $12.83/SF weighted-average base rent versus CBRE's $14.84/SF modeled market rent. Grocery Outlet is the reason to look: 16,650 SF doing $14.2 million of sales at $853 PSF and a computed 2.16% occupancy cost, one of only two grocers serving the trade area, and among the strongest grocery productivity in this portfolio. But its lease commenced only in November 2025 with a five-year primary term to October 2030 and the OM never prints the option structure — on 45% of the base rent, that is the first document to get. The value-add case is the 9,970 SF of vacancy, and CBRE's own 16-month absorption window is an honest signal that 8,780 SF of it is junior-box rather than small-shop space; the modeled jump from $488,776 to $680,675 of NOI between 2027 and 2028 carries $415,000 of tenant improvements and commissions behind it. The trade area supports the plan: 63,350 people within three miles at $91,662 average household income, a true trade area averaging $117,595, and a three-mile daytime population of 81,457 against 63,350 residents. Two cautions on the income itself. Smoker's Express pays $26.18/SF, 31% above CBRE's own market rent for space that size, with no sales disclosed — above-market rent that inflates the capitalized NOI and can reset down at its 2029 expiry — while three leases actually signed between 2024 and 2026 came in at $16.00 to $17.50/SF. And this is Pennsylvania, where the modeled $1.21/SF tax line is expressly unreassessed and the real exposure runs through Cumberland County's base-year assessment and its annually-republished Common Level Ratio rather than a sale-triggered reset.
